title: Descent of coefficient-compatible functors
statement:
Let $\Phi_E:\mathcal C_E(T)\to\mathcal C_E(S)$ be exact functors and let
$$
 \beta_{F/E}:T^S_{F/E}\Phi_E
 \xrightarrow{\sim}\Phi_FT^T_{F/E}
$$
be exact natural isomorphisms satisfying the unit, associator, and shift
equations of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. Then they induce an exact
functor $\Phi:\mathcal P_T\to\mathcal P_S$. On a representative
$u:T^T_{M/E}K\to T^T_{M/F}L$, its value is represented by
$$
 T^S_{M/E}\Phi_EK\xrightarrow{\beta_{M/E}}
 \Phi_MT^T_{M/E}K\xrightarrow{\Phi_M(u)}
 \Phi_MT^T_{M/F}L\xrightarrow{\beta_{M/F}^{-1}}
 T^S_{M/F}\Phi_FL.
$$
This functor is, by [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], already a functor on the
$\Qlb$ coefficient categories $\Dbc(T,\Qlb)=\mathcal P_T$ and
$\Dbc(S,\Qlb)=\mathcal P_S$. Compatible natural transformations and their
equations descend by the same formula.

In particular, the scalar-compatible families $(Rf_{*,E})_E$ and
$(Lg_E^*)_E$ descend to exact functors on $\Qlb$ coefficient categories, and
the finite-stage exchange maps descend to a natural transformation.

note:
*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this descent of functors: the
ledger's verified entries contain no filtered-colimit-of-categories
statement — the nearest, the Chapter 61 coefficient entries 09BS, 09BT, 09C1
and 09C7, work with one fixed Noetherian coefficient ring — and the
blueprint adds the descent of scalar-compatible exact functors and of their
natural transformations to the $\Qlb$ coefficient categories, together with
the descended direct images, pullbacks and exchange maps. The closest
descent statements in Stacks, each fetched and quoted, are the universal
properties of a localization and of a Verdier quotient: Lemma 13.5.7 ([Tag
05R7](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05R7), an exact functor out of
$\mathcal D$ that inverts the multiplicative system factors uniquely and
exactly through $S^{-1}\mathcal D$) and Lemma 13.6.8 ([Tag
05RJ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05RJ), the same for the quotient
$\mathcal D/\mathcal B$ by a full triangulated subcategory), with Definition
13.6.1 ([Tag 05RB](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05RB), saturated,
i.e. thick, triangulated subcategory) and Definition 13.6.7 ([Tag
05RI](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05RI),
$\mathcal D/\mathcal B=S^{-1}\mathcal D$). Difference: a localization or
quotient inverts a multiplicative system inside one category and its
factorization needs no further data, whereas $\mathcal P_T$ is a filtered
colimit of categories and the functors descend with the explicit
$\beta$-isomorphisms of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].

source.place: ## Proof, first sentence and displayed composite

proof.text:
Write $d_M(u)=\beta_{M/F,L}^{-1}\circ\Phi_M(u)\circ\beta_{M/E,K}$. For $M\subseteq N$ and $A\in\mathcal C_H(T)$ with $H\subseteq M$, the assumed associator equation for $\beta$ reads
$$\beta_{N/H,A}=\Phi_N(a^T_{N,M,H,A})\circ\beta_{N/M,T^T_{M/H}A}\circ T^S_{N/M}(\beta_{M/H,A})\circ(a^S_{N,M,H,\Phi_H A})^{-1}.$$
Naturality at $u$ reads
$$\Phi_N(T^T_{N/M}u)\circ\beta_{N/M,T^T_{M/E}K}=\beta_{N/M,T^T_{M/F}L}\circ T^S_{N/M}(\Phi_Mu).$$
Substitute the first equation at $(H,A)=(E,K),(F,L)$ and the pair-category formula $u_N=a^T_{N,M,F,L}\circ T^T_{N/M}(u)\circ(a^T_{N,M,E,K})^{-1}$ into $d_N(u_N)$. The inverse $\Phi_N(a^T_{N,M,F,L})$ cancels the left associator in $\Phi_N(u_N)$, and its right associator cancels $\Phi_N(a^T_{N,M,E,K})$. The displayed naturality equation then cancels the two remaining $\beta_{N/M}$ components, leaving
$$d_N(u_N)=a^S_{N,M,F,\Phi_FL}\circ T^S_{N/M}(d_M(u))\circ(a^S_{N,M,E,\Phi_EK})^{-1}.$$
This is exactly the target transport of $d_M(u)$. If $u_P=v_P$ witnesses equivalence, this equality gives equal target representatives $d_P(u_P)=d_P(v_P)$, so the assignment is well defined.

For the identity representative at $E$, the assumed unit equation $\beta_{E/E}=1$ gives $d_E(1_K)=1_{\Phi_EK}$. For composable maps $u:A\to B$ and $v:B\to C$ represented at one common stage $P$, the adjacent factors $\beta_{P/F,L}\circ\beta_{P/F,L}^{-1}$ cancel, giving $d_P(v)\circ d_P(u)=d_P(v\circ u)$. The transport equality of step 2 makes this calculation apply to the pair-category composition formula even when the initial stages differ. Also $d_P(u+v)=d_P(u)+d_P(v)$, since exact functors are additive and composition is bilinear. The common-stage calculus supplies the additive categories on which this is an additive functor.

Descend the stage shift comparison as a compatible transformation between the composites of the shift stage morphism and the given morphism. The betaCommShift equation is exactly Hom.comm after expanding the two composite comparisons. Its components are images of the finite-stage shift isomorphisms, hence yield a natural isomorphism on pair categories. Check zero and addition componentwise using the finite-stage CommShift laws and functor_map_ι. The comparison ιCompFunctorIso is compatible with this shift structure, because its components and the inclusion shift components are identities. By the common-stage distinguished-triangle criterion from [thm-weil-pbc-verdier-axioms], every distinguished source triangle is isomorphic to an included distinguished stage triangle. At that stage, the functor is exact, and the target inclusion is exact by the same Verdier theorem. Transport exactness through ιCompFunctorIso, then through mapTriangleCompIso and the given triangle isomorphism. Thus the descended functor preserves distinguished triangles. By [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] these are the required coefficient categories.

For another compatible family $\Psi$ with comparison $\gamma$, let $\eta_E:\Phi_E\to\Psi_E$ be a compatible natural transformation. Compatibility means
$$\eta_{M,T^T_{M/E}K}\circ\beta_{M/E,K}=\gamma_{M/E,K}\circ T^S_{M/E}(\eta_{E,K}).$$
Define $\eta_{(E,K)}=[E,\eta_{E,K}]$. At stage $M$ the naturality square for $[M,u]$ is the equality
$$T^S_{M/F}(\eta_{F,L})\circ d_M^\Phi(u)=d_M^\Psi(u)\circ T^S_{M/E}(\eta_{E,K}).$$
Indeed, the left side is $\gamma_{M/F,L}^{-1}\circ\eta_{M,T^T_{M/F}L}\circ\Phi_M(u)\circ\beta_{M/E,K}$. Naturality of $\eta_M$ replaces its middle two factors by $\Psi_M(u)\circ\eta_{M,T^T_{M/E}K}$; compatibility then gives the right side. Step 2 ensures the equality defines an equality of classes independent of the chosen stage. Identity transformations descend to identities and vertical composites descend to composites because their components are $[E,1]$ and $[E,\theta_{E,K}\circ\eta_{E,K}]$. For horizontally composed families, the comparison is $\Phi_M(\gamma_{M/E,K})\circ\beta_{M/E,\Psi_EK}$; substituting it into $d_M$ gives precisely the composite of the two descended assignments. Whiskering and horizontal composition therefore agree with finite-stage operations as well. Every equation between compatible transformations, formed with these operations, holds componentwise already at $E$, hence holds between the descended classes.

source.place: ## Proof, natural transformations and their equations sentence

proof.text: The finite-stage rational transport proposition supplies the exact functors $Rf_{*,E}$ and $Lg_E^*$ and their exchange transformation on $\Dbc(-,E)$ (with the integral-operation hypotheses required there). The scalar-extension proposition supplies their coherent comparison isomorphisms and states that scalar extension of the exchange map is the exchange map at the larger stage. These are respectively the hypotheses for steps 1–4 and the compatibility equation in step 5, so they give the asserted exact functors and exchange transformation on the Qbar categories.

proof.text:
Define $\Phi(E,K)=(E,\Phi_EK)$ on objects and, on a representative $(M,u)$,
by the displayed composite in $\mathcal C_M(S)$. The value is independent of
$M$: for $M\subset N$ the $\beta$-isomorphisms transport the composite for
$u$ to the composite for $u_N$, using the unit and associator equations of
[prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] which the $\beta$'s satisfy; equivalent
representatives give equal composites at the witnessing stage by those
equations, so $\Phi$ is well defined on the morphisms of
[def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. It is additive, the composites
being exact functors and exact natural isomorphisms of exact natural
transformations, and exact (finite-stage exactness of the $\Phi_E$ and the
$T$'s makes the composite exact on distinguished triangles); natural
transformations and their equations descend by that formula by the
equivariance with the $\beta$'s. By [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] this is
already the descent to the $\Qlb$ coefficient categories
($\Dbc(T,\Qlb)=\mathcal P_T$ and $\Dbc(S,\Qlb)=\mathcal P_S$); no extension
to an envelope is needed. The families $(Rf_{*,E})_E$ and $(Lg_E^*)_E$ carry
the scalar-extension isomorphisms of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] as the
data $\beta$, so they descend to exact functors on the $\Qlb$ coefficient
categories, and the finite-stage exchange maps, being compatible with scalar
extension, descend to a natural transformation.
